summary.intent: Fix a broken someguy IPNS routing service deployment on staging by diagnosing configuration issues and validating the fix via SDK E2E tests.
summary.outcome: Identified and fixed under-resourced someguy container config (missing port 4004, wrong DHT mode, low memory/CPU limits); all 83 SDK E2E tests pass with someguy as the IPNS routing backend; staging docker-compose, deploy workflow, and Alloy metrics config updated.

repo: someguy requires port 4004 exposed (TCP + UDP) for libp2p DHT peer discovery to function
someguy needs DHT mode 'accelerated' (not 'standard') and sufficient memory (1GB libp2p / 2GB container) for IPNS routing to work in staging
The API throttler uses a bypass header (x-throttle-bypass) controlled by THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET env var, not NODE_ENV=test
Vitest does not auto-load .env files into process.env — env vars must be passed explicitly or via a dotenv loader in vitest config
SDK E2E tests live in tests/sdk-e2e/ and require their own .env file mirroring THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET from the API
DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL in the API .env controls which routing backend is used; local dev uses a mock, staging should point to someguy at http://192.168.133.114:8190

code.finding: Throttler bypass is implemented as a guard that checks for a secret header, not via NODE_ENV — test suites must send the header to avoid 429s
The SDK axios instance forwards defaultHeaders to every request, so setting the bypass header in client config is sufficient
No dotenv plugin configured — env vars from .env files are not loaded automatically, requiring explicit CLI injection
Test harness reads THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET from process.env and sets it as a default header on the SDK client
someguy service config updated: added port 4004 TCP+UDP, accelerated DHT mode, increased memory to 2GB, CPU to 1.0, start period to 60s

workflow: When E2E tests show 429s, first suspect throttle bypass config before investigating rate limit logic
For vitest-based E2E suites, passing env vars explicitly on the CLI (VAR=value npx vitest) is more reliable than .env files unless dotenv is explicitly configured
DHT-based services (someguy/Kubo) need a warm-up period after startup before routing table is populated — allow 2+ minutes before testing IPNS resolve

friction: NODE_ENV=test had no effect on throttling — the actual mechanism (bypass header) was not obvious without reading the guard source
Vitest silently ignores .env files, causing the bypass secret to not be loaded even after creating the .env file — required a second debugging round
429 failures looked identical whether caused by missing bypass header or insufficient bypass propagation, making root cause diagnosis slow
Had to discover the throttle bypass mechanism by grepping source rather than from docs or comments
open_items: vitest.config.ts for sdk-e2e has no dotenv plugin — consider adding @dotenvx/dotenvx or vite-plugin-env-compatible so .env files work as expected
The staging someguy fix has been committed but not yet deployed — needs a deploy run to validate in actual staging environment
Consider documenting the THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET pattern and E2E test setup in a README or CONTRIBUTING guide to avoid repeating this debugging cycle
